answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake bond before it can trade. Think of the bond as timber an agent must mill itself: cheap for one real agent, ruinous to fake a thousand. Honest agents that behave well keep their stake and earn fees; a mesa of fake identities collapses because every clone must pay the same bond up front, and misbehavior slashes it. New agents start in a low-trust oasis with capped volume until they build a history, so an attacker pays full price for every fake account and gains almost nothing before being caught.
